newsitem.title: JAPAN: Firms plan Japan distribution tie-up - paper.
newsitem.headline: Firms plan Japan distribution tie-up - paper.

text.p: A number of major manufacturers and retailers operating in Japan plan to cooperate to cut distribution and inventory costs, a Japanese business daily said on Thursday.

The Nihon Keizai Shimbun said 24 companies have already decided to join the project, including retailers such as Daiei Inc and Ito-Yokado Co Ltd, and producers such as Kao Corp, Procter & Gamble Co, Kirin Brewery Co Ltd and Ajinomoto Co Inc.
The companies were not immediately available to comment on the report.

The paper said 30 companies were eventually expected to participate in the project, under which they would standardise product codes, set up common distribution centres and jointly deliver their products.
They will form a study group on August 1 and aim to start trial joint distribution in early 1998, the paper said.
